description: Structuring software at the class and system level: design principles such as SOLID, coupling and cohesion, the creational, structural and behavioural design patterns, architectural styles from layered to event-driven and microservices, quality attributes and their trade-offs, and documenting and evaluating architecture. Every pattern is implemented, refactored into and tested in the browser code lab, and every style is exercised on a running system whose behaviour under load and failure students can observe.
modelledOn: Gamma, Helm, Johnson and Vlissides, Design Patterns: Elements of Reusable Object-Oriented Software
Bass, Clements and Kazman, Software Architecture in Practice
outcomes: Apply SOLID and related design principles to reduce coupling, increase cohesion and refactor code smells.
Select, implement and justify creational, structural and behavioural design patterns for a given design problem.
Compare architectural styles and choose one, or a combination, that fits a system's requirements and constraints.
Analyse quality attributes with scenarios and apply architectural tactics to meet them, explaining the trade-offs.
Document an architecture with multiple views and decision records and evaluate it with a structured method.

units.title: Design principles: SOLID, coupling and cohesion
topics: Modularity, information hiding and abstraction; kinds of coupling and cohesion
SOLID: single responsibility, open-closed, Liskov substitution, interface segregation and dependency inversion
Composition over inheritance; the law of Demeter; DRY and YAGNI
UML class and sequence diagrams as design notation
Code smells and refactoring; refactoring towards patterns

units.title: Creational patterns
topics: Factory method and abstract factory
Builder and prototype
Singleton and why it is often an anti-pattern; testability concerns
Dependency injection and inversion-of-control containers
Object pools and lazy initialisation

units.title: Structural patterns
topics: Adapter: wrapping several mobile money provider APIs behind one payment interface
Facade and proxy: simplifying subsystems; remote, caching and protection proxies
Decorator: adding logging, retries and caching without subclassing
Composite and bridge
Flyweight and memory-conscious design for low-end devices
Comparing similar patterns: adapter, decorator, proxy and facade

units.title: Behavioural patterns
topics: Strategy and template method: pluggable fare-calculation rules for tro-tro routes
Observer and publish-subscribe; event handling in user interfaces
Command, memento and undo; chain of responsibility
State: modelling a transaction life cycle as a state machine
Iterator, mediator and visitor; interpreter in brief
Anti-patterns and pattern overuse

units.title: Architectural styles: layered, event-driven, microservices
topics: What architecture is: structures, views, components and connectors
Layered, client-server and pipe-and-filter styles; MVC and MVVM
Hexagonal (ports and adapters) and clean architecture
Event-driven architecture: message brokers, event sourcing and CQRS
Microservices versus the modular monolith; service boundaries and domain-driven design
Serverless and peer-to-peer styles in brief

units.title: Quality attributes and trade-offs
topics: Quality attribute scenarios: source, stimulus, environment, response and response measure
Tactics for availability, performance and scalability
Tactics for security, modifiability, testability and usability
Consistency and partition tolerance: the CAP theorem and eventual consistency
Designing for intermittent power and low bandwidth: offline queues, caching, retries and idempotent operations
Cost, time to market and team structure as architectural forces; Conway's law

units.title: Patterns for distributed systems
topics: API gateway, service discovery and backend-for-frontend
Resilience patterns: circuit breaker, bulkhead, timeout and retry with backoff
Data management: database per service, sagas and the outbox pattern
Migrating legacy systems with the strangler fig pattern

units.title: Documenting and evaluating architecture
topics: Views and viewpoints: the 4+1 view model and the C4 model
Architecture decision records and documenting rationale
Evaluation with ATAM: utility trees, sensitivity points and risks
Architecture fitness functions and conformance checking in code
Technical debt and architectural erosion
Capstone: design, document and evaluate the architecture for a city transport and fare-payment platform
